details.summary: This is an exceptional, highly functional recipe that beautifully adapts a creamy stroganoff profile into a high-fiber, plant-protein-forward meal. The use of a ready-to-eat farro pouch and the off-heat yogurt technique show smart culinary design that honors the 30-minute rule and the dual-condition nutrition brief.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is excellent and highly coherent. The combination of earthy mushrooms, thyme, Dijon, and tangy Greek yogurt beautifully mimics a classic stroganoff or fricassee while remaining completely aligned with the diet's principles.
Every listed ingredient is properly used in the steps, and no unlisted ingredients appear.

The steps are well written and include visual cues, but the cook time header (8 minutes) only reflects the minimum possible time (5+1+2). Update the cook time header to 11 minutes (7+1+3) to reflect the maximum range. Additionally, add a 'Check at 5 minutes' prompt to step 2 to strictly follow the minimum-time-check rule.
The French-inspired American profile is accurately represented through the fricassee technique and classic pairing of mushrooms, Dijon, and thyme.

The skillet method is perfect. The instruction to remove from heat and let cool slightly before adding the nonfat Greek yogurt is an essential and correctly executed culinary technique to prevent curdling.
The macros compute accurately. Lentils, farro, and a generous portion of nonfat Greek yogurt perfectly explain the high protein (29.8 g) and fiber (12.7 g) counts without meat.
The title and intro accurately reflect the dish. The phrase 'liver-friendly' safely communicates the book's intent without triggering any banned 'detox' or 'cure' language.
Highly appealing. It offers a fast, comforting, creamy, and filling weekday meal using common pantry staples.

This is a textbook example of a recipe serving both conditions simultaneously: it relies on high-quality complex carbs (farro, lentils) for blood sugar control, while utilizing plant protein and eliminating heavy cream to manage saturated fat for the liver.

Added sugar is strictly zero. The carbohydrate load (53.3 g) is exceptionally high quality, derived entirely from whole grains, legumes, and dairy, landing perfectly in the top end of the tier's window.
Perfectly hits the 'Vegetable & Meatless Dinners' intent. Using Greek yogurt alongside lentils to comfortably clear the 26 g plant-based protein floor is a smart, targeted design choice.
Easily achieved in under 30 minutes from a cold start. Utilizing a ready-to-eat cooked farro pouch is exactly the kind of smart, declared shortcut this book encourages.
